headline: Sales return to growth, margins expand
summary_short: Estée Lauder's fiscal Q4/full-year FY2026 results showed net sales up 6.3% y/y to $3,627M in the quarter (organic +5%) and $15,049M for the year (organic +3%), with adjusted diluted EPS of $0.39 (quarter) and $2.51 (year), while GAAP results swung to a full-year profit of $0.50/share from a $(3.15) loss a year earlier.
summary_long: Sales grew across every category except Hair Care and every region in Q4, aided by North America's return to growth, partly offset by Middle East disruption. Gross margin expanded 150bp for the year on PRGP savings and sales leverage, offset by inflation and tariffs. Full-year GAAP operating income swung to +$780M from -$785M, mainly because prior-year impairments and Talcum charges didn't repeat, partly offset by higher restructuring charges and an $84M litigation contingency. Free cash flow rose to $1,316M (from $670M) on higher operating cash flow and lower capex. Cash rose to $3,498M after dividends and a TOM FORD payment. For fiscal 2027, EL affirmed 3%-5% organic sales growth and raised adjusted operating margin outlook to 12.7%-13.5%.

drivers.explanation: Growth across all product categories except Hair Care and all geographic regions; North America's return to growth included an $18M one-time gift-card liability reversal, partly offset by Middle East conflict disruption.
PRGP operational efficiencies (procurement, expense optimization, lower excess/obsolescence) and sales leverage, partially offset by inflation and incremental tariffs net of refunds received.

Prior year carried $1,286M of goodwill/intangible impairments and $159M of Talcum litigation charges that did not repeat, partially offset by $337M higher restructuring charges and an $84M securities-settlement loss contingency this year.
Operating leverage and gross-margin expansion, including PRGP benefits that funded increased consumer-facing investment while non-consumer-facing expense stayed flat.
Quarter's GAAP loss reflects $306M ($.71/share) of restructuring and other charges and an $.08 Middle East drag; adjusted EPS also benefited from a $.07 tariff-refund gain.
Operating cash flow rose 39% to $1,773M on higher net earnings, while capital expenditures fell to $457M from $602M as the company prioritized consumer-facing investment.
Higher operating cash flow and lower capex drove the increase, partially offset by $508M of dividends paid and a $300M TOM FORD deferred-consideration payment.
CEO Stéphane de La Faverie cited a fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating organic growth and "significant operating margin expansion" under the Beauty Reimagined and One ELC operating model.
